title: Variables, terms and expressions
competency: Describe terms and expressions, and simplify algebraic expressions with and without brackets.

keywords.def: A number, a variable, or a product or quotient of a number and a variable.
The number factor of a term. In −3xy it is −3.
Terms with exactly the same variables and exponents, like 3x and −5x.
A term with no variable, like 4 or −5.
Numbers and letters joined by +, −, × or ÷, like 2x − 3.
a(b + c) = ab + ac. Multiply each term in the bracket.

en.text: A term is a number, a variable, or a number times or divided by a variable. 4, xy and 3x/y are terms. x − y is two terms. The numerical coefficient is the number factor: in 6ab it is 6, in x it is 1.

screens.title: One piece or two?
screens.ask: Which of these is ONE term?
screens.after: −3x is one term: a number times a variable. 2x + 3 and x + y are two terms joined by + .

screens.title: Definition 3.2
paras: A term can be a constant (a number) or a variable.
A term can also be a product or quotient of a number and a variable.

screens.title: Example 1: a term or not?
screens.ask: Tap each one. Is it one term?
items: A term: a product of two variables.
Not one term: − joins two terms, 12xy and −4.
Not one term: it has two terms, x and −y.

screens.title: Definition 3.3
paras: Look at a product of a number and a variable.
Its number factor is called the numerical coefficient.

screens.title: Example 2: find the coefficient
screens.ask: Tap each term to see its numerical coefficient.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A number, a variable, or a product or quotient of a number and a variable.
The number factor of a term. In −3xy it is −3.

screens.text: Find the numerical coefficient of the term −3x.
screens.why:
−3x means (−3) × x.
The number factor is −3.
Keep the minus sign with the number.
3 is wrong: it drops the sign.
screens.clue: Keep the sign with the number.

screens.why:
A term is one piece: a number, a letter, or a product or quotient of them.
4 and 0 are constants, so they are terms.
xy is a product and 3x/y is a quotient: terms.
12xy − 4 and 5x − 4y have a − joining two parts.
So each of them is two terms, not one term.
screens.clue: Look for a + or − sign between parts.
screens.text: Sort each one: is it a single term?

screens.ask: Find the numerical coefficient: in −z it is ___
screens.why:
−z means (−1) × z.
The 1 is not written, but it is there.
Keep the minus sign.
The coefficient is −1.
screens.clue: What number is hidden in front of z?

screens.ask: Find the numerical coefficient: in y/2 it is ___
screens.why:
y/2 means y ÷ 2.
Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 1/2.
So y/2 = (1/2) × y.
The coefficient is 1/2.
screens.clue: Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 1/2.

screens.ask: Find the coefficient: in 5 − 3x²y, the numerical coefficient of x²y is ___
screens.why:
5 − 3x²y has two terms: 5 and −3x²y.
The term with x²y is −3x²y.
−3x²y = (−3) × x²y.
The coefficient is −3, with its sign.
The 2 is an exponent, not a coefficient.
screens.clue: Find the term that has x²y. Keep its sign.

en.text: Like terms have exactly the same variables with the same exponents. 3x and −5x are like terms. 3x² and 2x³ are unlike. Order of letters does not matter: 3xy and 3yx are like. All constant terms are like terms.

screens.title: Oranges and bananas
screens.ask: Which pair can be put together into one term?
screens.after: 3x + 2x = 5x, like 3 oranges and 2 oranges. 3x and 2y are like oranges and bananas.

screens.title: Definition 3.4
paras: Like terms have exactly the same variables and exponents. Their numerical coefficients may differ.
Terms which are not like terms are called unlike terms.
A term with no variable is a constant term. All constant terms are like terms.
screens.note: 3x is the same as 3x¹. In 5x², the exponent is 2.

screens.title: Example 3
screens.ask: Tap each pair: like or unlike?
items: Like: the same letters a, b, c, each with exponent 1.
Like: yx is the same as xy.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Terms with exactly the same variables and exponents, like 3x and −5x.
A term with no variable, like 4 or −5.

screens.text: Like terms: true or false? 3xy and 3yx are like terms.
screens.why:
yx means y × x, and y × x = x × y.
So 3yx = 3xy.
Both have x¹ and y¹.
Same variables, same exponents: like terms. True.
screens.clue: Does the order of letters matter?

screens.why:
Like terms need the same letters with the same exponents.
3x and −5x are both x¹: like.
xy² and y²x are both x¹y²: like.
20xy and ab have different letters: unlike.
3x² and 2x³, −80ab and 15a²b²: exponents differ, unlike.
screens.clue: Compare the letters, then the exponents.
screens.text: Sort each pair: like terms or unlike terms?
Like terms: true or false? 3a²b and 3ab² are like terms.
screens.why:
In 3a²b, a has exponent 2 and b has exponent 1.
In 3ab², a has exponent 1 and b has exponent 2.
The exponents do not match.
So they are unlike terms. False.
screens.clue: Check the exponent of a in each.

screens.text: Like terms: which term is like 4x²y?
screens.why:
4x²y has x² and y¹.
−yx² = −x²y: also x² and y¹. Like!
4xy² has x¹ and y²: unlike.
4x² has no y, and x²y² has y²: unlike.
The coefficient (−1 or 4) does not matter.
screens.clue: Rewrite each term with x first. Compare exponents.

en.text: An algebraic expression uses numbers, letters and +, −, ×, ÷. Its terms are the parts joined by + or −. One term is a monomial, two terms a binomial, three terms a trinomial. In 3x + 2a − 5 the terms are 3x, 2a and −5.

screens.title: Count the terms
screens.after: The parts joined by + or − are 3x, 2a and −5. That is 3 terms.

screens.title: Definition 3.5
paras: Algebraic expressions use numbers, letters and +, −, × and ÷.
The terms of an expression are the parts joined by plus or minus signs.

screens.title: Definitions 3.6–3.8
screens.ask: Tap each name to see how many terms it has.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Numbers and letters joined by +, −, × or ÷, like 2x − 3.

screens.text: Name the expression by its number of terms: 5x − 3y − 4 is a:
screens.why:
Split the expression at the + and − signs.
The terms are 5x, −3y and −4.
That is 3 terms.
Three terms make a trinomial.
screens.clue: Count the parts joined by + or −.

screens.why:
Count the terms joined by + or −.
24 and 5x have one term each: monomials.
−21t − 2x and 20w + w² have two terms: binomials.
z − y − 25x and 3x − 2y + 1 have three: trinomials.
screens.text: Sort each expression: monomial, binomial or trinomial?

screens.ask: Find the constant term: in 3x − 2y + 1 it is ___
screens.why:
The terms are 3x, −2y and 1.
3x and −2y have letters.
1 has no letter.
So the constant term is 1.

screens.text: Simplify first, then name it: 3x + 5 − 3x + y is a:
screens.why:
Collect the x terms: 3x − 3x = 0.
What is left is y + 5.
y + 5 has two terms.
Two terms make a binomial.
Trinomial is tempting, but count after simplifying.

en.text: To simplify: remove brackets with the distributive property, collect like terms, then add or subtract their coefficients. Watch the signs: −2(x − 4) = −2x + 8. Unlike terms cannot be added.

screens.title: Simplifying algebraic expressions
paras: Remove brackets using the distributive property.

screens.title: Note
screens.ask: Tap each rule to see an example.
items: Add or subtract the coefficients of like terms
Be careful of signs with brackets

screens.title: Key words
defs: a(b + c) = ab + ac. Multiply each term in the bracket.

screens.why:
The x terms are 3x and −8x.
3x − 8x = (3 − 8)x = −5x.
35y has no like term, so it stays.
Answer: −5x + 35y.
30xy is wrong: unlike terms cannot be added.

The b terms: 21b − 32b = (21 − 32)b = −11b.
The numbers: 15 + 3 = 18.
Answer: −11b + 18.
screens.clue: Group the b terms and the numbers.

screens.why:
Multiply each term inside by −2.
−2 × x = −2x.
−2 × (−4) = +8 (same signs give +).
Answer: −2x + 8.
−2x − 8 forgets that − × − = +.

Remove the bracket: 3(3x − 6y) = 9x − 18y.
Now we have 9x − 18y + x + 18y − 4.
x terms: 9x + x = 10x.
y terms: −18y + 18y = 0.
Answer: 10x − 4.

2(3a − b) = 6a − 2b.
−3(a − 2b) = −3a + 6b, because −3 × (−2b) = +6b.
a terms: 6a − 3a = 3a.
b terms: −2b + 6b = 4b.
Answer: 3a + 4b.

math.integer-signs.name: Signs when multiplying and adding integers

screens.title: Integer signs
steps: Adding different signs: −5 + 3 = −2 (take 3 from 5, keep the sign of 5).

screens.why:
Both numbers are negative: the signs are the same.
Same signs give a positive answer.
3 × 4 = 12.
So (−3) × (−4) = 12. (−12 would need different signs.)
screens.clue: Are the signs the same or different?

items.why:
3x has x¹. −5x has x¹.
Same letter, same exponent.
The coefficients 3 and −5 may differ.
So they are like terms.

items.text: Like or unlike? 20xy and ab are:
items.why:
20xy has the letters x and y.
ab has the letters a and b.
The letters are different.
So they are unlike terms.

items.text: Like or unlike? xy² and y²x are:
items.why:
y²x = x × y², which is the same as xy².
Both have x¹ and y².
The order of letters does not matter.
So they are like terms.
items.clue: Order of letters does not matter.

items.why:
3x² has x with exponent 2.
2x³ has x with exponent 3.
Same letter, but the exponents differ.
So they are unlike terms.

3/x = 3 × 1/x.
5/x = 5 × 1/x.
Both have the same variable part, 1/x.
So they are like terms.

items.text: Term or not? Is (2x − y)/5 a single term?
items.why:
Divide each part by 5.
(2x − y)/5 = 2x/5 − y/5.
A − sign joins two parts.
So it is two terms, not one. No.

items.ask: Find the numerical coefficient: in −4x it is ___
items.why:
−4x means (−4) × x.
The number factor is −4.
Keep the sign.
The coefficient is −4.

items.ask: Find the numerical coefficient: in 3x/4 it is ___
items.why:
3x/4 means 3x ÷ 4.
This is (3/4) × x.
The number factor is 3/4.
The coefficient is 3/4 = 0.75.

items.text: Name the expression and its constant term: 24
items.why:
24 is one term, so it is a monomial.
24 has no letter.
So 24 is also the constant term.
Monomial; constant term 24.
items.clue: Count terms. Is there a number term?

items.text: Name the expression and its constant term: 5x − 3y − 4
items.why:
The terms are 5x, −3y and −4.
Three terms make a trinomial.
The term with no letter is −4.
Keep its minus sign: the constant term is −4.
items.clue: Keep the sign of the constant.

items.text: Collect like terms: simplify 3z − 12 − 11y + x + y − 48z − 3.
items.why:
x terms: only x.
y terms: −11y + y = −10y.
z terms: 3z − 48z = −45z.
Numbers: −12 − 3 = −15.
Answer: x − 10y − 45z − 15.
items.clue: Group each letter, then the numbers.

items.text: Remove the brackets and simplify: −3(−a + 6) + x − (z + 4) − 2x.

items.why:
x² terms: 3x² − x² = 2x².
x terms: 4x − 3x = x.
Numbers: 6 − 3 = 3.
x² and x are unlike, so they stay apart.
Answer: 2x² + x + 3.

items.text: Remove the brackets and simplify: 5(2 − x²) − 3(x² − 4y).

test.ask: Find the numerical coefficient: in 7ab it is ___
test.why:
7ab = 7 × a × b.
The number factor is 7.
So the coefficient is 7.

test.text: Like terms: true or false? 2 and −5 are like terms.
test.why:
2 and −5 have no variable.
They are constant terms.
All constant terms are like terms.
True.

test.text: Count the terms: which expression is a binomial?
test.why:
A binomial has exactly two terms.
5x + 3y has the terms 5x and 3y: two terms.
12ab has one term. x − y − z has three.
So 5x + 3y is the binomial.

4(x + 3y) = 4x + 12y.
Now we have 20 + 4x + 12y − 4x − 8y.
x terms: 4x − 4x = 0.
y terms: 12y − 8y = 4y.
Answer: 4y + 20.
